body.x: The CES keynote is very dramatic. Would itbe fair to say that it is more exciting than Hollywood-made Science Fiction(SF) movies? Oh, CES Keynote is a science nonfiction movie because it dealswith real situations. At least, the opening keynote will not be wrong if youthink you are watching the 'Science Nonfiction' movie.

It's been a long time, but Microsoft's BillGates keynote, which has been on the CES Opening Keynote for decades, and CEOBrian Krzanich Keynote since 2014. It is no exaggeration to say that theiropening keynote has made CES one of the largest exhibitions.

Bill Gates and Brian Krzanich built their own technology and products to be used in future worlds, demonstrating or demonstrating in front of thousands of reporters. The marvelous scenes created by the technology have gotten people to be inspired, and also sometimes cheering and sometimes shocked.

I still remember the keynote scene fiveyears ago. In the pre-show keynote of 2014, when Intel CEO Brian Krzanich firstappeared on the stage with the CES opening keynote speaker, which is a scenethat will never be forgotten. The concept of AR (Augmented Reality) was still astrange thing at the time. At the keynote stage, the whale monster"Leviathan" actually floated up and strolled over the keynote seatedby thousands of people. Those who directly saw the "AugmentedReality" could not believe what they were seeing as if they had seen a UFO.

As the monster whale actually floated in the air as if it were swimming in the ocean, the audience shook hands to touch the whale that came over their heads. There were also people who put the gestures of a huge but flexible whale on their iPad or camera. The whale swimmer's whirlwind, which could be seen perfectly in any angle, was more realistic and "exciting" than any magic. Watching a video of the keynote scene would be much better than explaining it in thousands of words. Please click on the following link to YouTube.
(Reference image 1. Leviathan at Intel CES 2014 Keynote)

In recent years, with the rapid development of AI and other IT technologies, as well as the development of video technology and stage technology, the opening keynote has become brilliant and the production has become very bold. This is the story of Intel CEO Brian Krzanich. At the opening keynote of CES 2018, but helicopter-sized passenger drones that can carry people were shown on stage, and it was the world's first time to see 100 drones fly in the room with AI technology.
(References 2, 3. Monte Carlo Hotel 'Park Theater' stage preparation and rehearsal scene)
(Reference image 4. Intel drones shootingstar world's first 100 indoor flight success: Guinness world record)

Do they only emphasize 'technology' in CESkeynote? It's not like that. It also shows that technology can create beautifulart. You will see how Intel creates sensorial, data transmission, graphics andLED lighting technologies to create a spectacular and dreamy stage. It is worthnoting that the dancer transforms the various gestures and movements created bydancers wearing their sensors on their ankles and wrists into data andexpressing them three-dimensionally on the screen.

Since the original image (2D) is expressedin a plane and the scene shown by the camera angle is limited, there is a limitto feel the impression of the scene as it is, but the next image alone isenough to create a process I can feel it. It is a unique scene that cannot beshown in any broadcasting station or movie.

There are three major shows that are most famous in Las Vegas. They are the O (O) show of the Bellagio Hotel, the KA show of MGM Grand Hotel, Le Reve show of the Wynn Hotel. Compared to these shows, I found Intel keynote scenes to be newer, more creative, and much more inspiring.
(See video 5. Intel CES 2018 Keynote |Amazing LED Technology Pre-show feat. Dancer @ sophiesantella)

However, the opening keynote of Intel CEOBrian Krzanich, who made his keynote debut for the fourth year, will no longerbe available at CES 2019. This is because he retired from his position as CEOseveral months ago. The reason for his resignation is that he broke the rulesprohibiting in-house dating. In the background of his sudden resignation, wecan read Intel's very strict corporate culture.

The other side estimates that one of the reasonsfor Brian's departure was that Intel's crisis persisted after Brian took overas CEO in 2013. Samsung, Qualcomm, and Huawei have started to lead the marketas the market has moved from PC to mobile, and Intel has invested heavily inmobile, but its past reputation is not enough to overturn the market and thecrisis ended in Intel firing 12,000 employees. There was a report in Novembersaying that Brian Krzanich was elected CEO and president of CDK Global, acompany that develops automobile-related software.

This is presumptuous, but I think the CESwas suddenly bewildered by the sudden resignation of Intel CEO and theinability to appear on the keynote stage. As the proverb says, 'the beginningis half'. In fact the success of the CES depends on the opening keynote.Thousands of reporters from over 150 countries around the world are writinghundreds of thousands of articles on Opening Keynotes, so the Opening Keynotehas a huge impact on the overall show.

By the way, the main character of theopening keynote of CES 2019 was announced as the CTO of LG Electronics, Il-pyeongPark (English name I.P. Park). The theme of the keynote is called 'AI for andEven Better Life'. CES has just released a press release about the openingkeynote from mid-October, and I think it's because of the backlog of Intel CEOsthat there's been a lot of vacancies and that they've gotten in a hurry.

On the LG side, Park Il-pyeong CTO gave akeynote speech on AI at IFA 2018 in Berlin, Germany in early September. So LGclaims that Park giving a keynote speech at CES 2019, is 'showing a globalstatus of LG in the AI ​​field'. However IFA and CES’ 'Class' is verydifferent. So I think that there is a behind story regarding this selectionsince CES would not just simply re-use the contents which was already opened ata lower-grade (?) Exhibition.

At the CES 2018 press conference, Park Il-pyeong, CTO of LG Electronics, presented a presentation on 'AI - LG ThinQ'. The IFA 2018 story in September was probably the same as the story he had at CES 2018. So I am guessing the CES 2019 opening keynote will be nearly the same as the stories he told before. This hints that the opening keynote of CES 2019 will not be as exciting. Of course, this assumption comes from my personal experience of visiting the CES opening keynote for the past 14 years.
( See video 6. LG at IFA 2018 - IFA keynote speech)
(Reference image 7. Summary image of CES2018 LG Press Conference)

But for the first time ever, LG has been theprotagonist of the CES opening keynote stage, and hopefully will show yousomething new. Perhaps the people will be preparing all day and night. I personallywant to show LG's advertising model 'BTS (Bulletproof Boys)' on stage. I do notknow if this idea will come true, but I think the effect of LG promotion willbe enormous if 'BTS' comes on stage with thousands of reporters from over 150countries watching.

If we can make 'LG' brand equal to 'BTS', itwill help brand awareness in the global market. Thousands of reporters havewritten articles, but the effect of the images and pictures of the scene willproduce a big hit. If you have already opened the same story about 'AI' twice, thechances are, you will not be able to show anything special. So instead, mightas well plan a keynote with 'BTS.'

I finish the second story of today. Thereare some people who have to see the opening keynote. I have visited the CESseveral times, but the people who visited the exhibition hall, the politicians,the heads of local governments, the heads of public agencies, and CEOs of allcompanies look forward to the opening keynote and get an inspiration to createinnovation. Please read the big picture (Mega Trend) rather than trying tounderstand the details. But there is one thing to note. Originally, Keynote isa place made for reporters, so if you are not a journalist you should go earlyand line up. If you go late, you cannot get into your seat.

Of course, you can do all of your production by yourself on your own smartphone. The reason for making a documentary on smartphone was to use it as lecture (educational use) material.

I think that it is best to present the vivid scene with visual images in the flow of global industry, knowledge of new technology or new product, and information transmission. By doing it all by yourself, you can save on production costs. Generally, if you make 50 ~ 60 minute documentary, you have to invest a lot of manpower and cost from planning stage to production completion.

I hope that there will be more opportunitiesfor me to create a documentary for those who cannot participate in the CES,that is, those who cannot get on the spacecraft to the future world.
